title: Products and inventory foundation for POS
userNeed: A retailer needs to create sellable products and know the available stock before using checkout.
acceptance: A workspace can create, search, edit, archive, and restore products with variants, tenant-unique SKUs, optional barcodes, and integer minor-unit prices.
Owners and admins can receive stock and correct counts with a required reason; members can view but cannot modify stock.
Each stock operation records an append-only movement and changes the balance in one transaction without allowing negative stock.
Products, variants, stores, stock balances, and movements are isolated by tenant in the API and database.
A new workspace gets a default Main store; existing workspaces receive one through migration.
verification: Frontend lint, typecheck, build and backend vet, build, tests pass.
Run migrations 0014 and 0015 on the owner's local database, then smoke-test create product, receive 5, count 3, edit SKU/price, archive/restore, member permissions, and cross-workspace isolation.
rollout: Current implementation is on feature/products-inventory. The owner applies migrations 0014 and 0015 locally and performs the browser smoke test before merging.

title: POS cash checkout MVP with atomic stock deduction
userNeed: A cashier needs to sell stocked products quickly and give the customer a clear receipt while inventory remains accurate.
acceptance: An authorized cashier can search or scan a variant, add it to a cart, change quantity, and remove it from the cart.
Checkout shows line totals, grand total, cash received, and change in the workspace currency. Prices are captured on the sale and do not change after product edits.
Confirming a cash sale creates one order with line items and payment and records linked sale stock movements in one tenant-scoped transaction.
Concurrent or repeated checkout requests cannot oversell, duplicate a sale, or make stock negative; insufficient stock returns an actionable error.
The cashier can open a receipt for the completed sale. A failed sale leaves stock and payment unchanged.
Taxes, discounts, returns, offline checkout, and split payments are explicitly outside this first slice.
verification: Add automated tests for totals, stock decrement, retry/idempotency, insufficient stock, concurrent checkout, tenant isolation, and cashier permissions.
Run frontend checks, backend checks, and migration checks. Manually sell one item, inspect the receipt and movement ledger, then verify stock changes only once.
rollout: Depends on the Products and inventory foundation issue and migrations 0014/0015. Any new sales migration requires owner-run local migration and human review before merge.
